Civic News Company is leading a civic revival.

We were founded to address one of the most consequential market failures of our time: the collapse of local news. Since 2008, nearly two-thirds of U.S. newsroom jobs have disappeared, leaving communities without trusted reporting on education, elections, and public health. Our mission is simple and urgent: to help people understand how America works so they can make it work better.

ThroughChalkbeat(education),Votebeat(elections), andHealthbeat(public health), we operate a national network of local news bureaus that combine deep local expertise with centralized national infrastructure.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Civic News is seeking aReporterto cover schools and education policy as part of the Chalkbeat Indiana team.

This is a critical moment to report about education in Indianapolis. How the city’s schools are run and governed is going through a radical transformation, with shifting power dynamics and uncertainty over how it will play out in the city’s district-run and charter schools. Changes to how school performance is measured, decisions about students’transportation to and from school, and charged debates about school closures all loom on the horizon.

You will tell these stories, hold leaders accountable, and put the news into context for students and families.Your work will help families and leaders make decisions for stronger public understanding of the institutions and decisions that shape students' lives. You’ll also be a member of a team covering education across Indiana, including how high schools prepare students for college and career, and what access families have to vouchers and online schools.

Capturing this story requires strong beat reporting, source development, relationship-building, and writing skills. You should enjoy a fast-paced and newsy environment and be comfortable as one of Chalkbeat’s public faces in the community and representing the organization at public events and on social media. This role includes night meeting coverage as well as the occasional evening event.

The key responsibilities for this role include:

• Report and write compelling local education stories, balancing quick-turn news coverage with enterprise and accountability journalism.

• Develop and execute longer-term reporting projects that deepen readers’ understanding of local education issues.

• Serve as a trusted guide for readers by clearly explaining how education systems, policies, and decisions affect local communities.

• Hold public officials and institutions accountable through rigorous, fair, and well-sourced reporting.

• Engage with readers and community members to identify relevant stories, questions, and areas of interest.

• Collaborate with colleagues across Chalkbeat and with external news partners on reporting and special projects, including TV, radio and panel appearances.

• Build and maintain relationships with a broad range of sources, including educators, education leaders, parents, students, and community members.

• Report stories that make an impact in the community and drive change.

What background and skills do you have? (We know not all strong candidates will have all the skills we list. That’s OK. What else do you bring to the table? Please tell us!): The person we seek:

• 3+ years of experience in journalism.

• Excellent news judgment.

• Breaking news metabolism and decisiveness.

• Ability to produce ambitious, agenda-setting enterprise journalism.

• Strong interpersonal skills, demonstrating empathy and understanding while being unafraid to have tough conversations when needed.

• Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion.

• Passion for education and Chalkbeat’s mission is a must; knowledge of education is a strong plus, but not required.

Our UX apprentices work through the end-to-end UX design and UX research process for a startup idea of their choice that will help them attract hiring managers in that topic space or industry.

This apprenticeship program is open to new grads and UX career changers alike! Here are some apprenticeship requirements to keep in mind before applying:
Interested in creative tech career paths in UX research, UX design, product design or service design
Willing to commit 5-10 hours of work per week to complete program deliverables
Willing to attend 2-3 hour weekend lectures to learn the end-to-end design process OR willing to complete online video course modules
Open to feedback from UX mentors and demonstrates a willingness to revise design work
Apprenticeship Program Learnings:
Build digital products and services 0-1
Lead end-to-end design process for a startup idea or topic of your choice
Lead product scoping and feature scoping, as well as entire project management
Identify target market for product and position product for launch success
Develop a business model for the product or service and demonstrate how the product/service will scale as the business model scales
Lead discovery research by managing user recruitment, creating research plans, writing interview guides, leading 8-16 discovery interviews, and synthesizing interview insights
Deliver a compelling UX design and business pitch for your startup idea, showcasing both qualitative and quantitative data to justify the problem space and the solution
Tell a compelling story about users by showcasing user types, personas, stakeholder maps, journey maps, process maps, service blueprints, ideation matrixes, sketches, wireframes, UX workflows, prototypes and other visual deliverables
Lead user testing of wireframes and prototypes to improve product/service usability and constantly iterate on your startup idea
Design a unique design system for your solution from scratch, creating components, a style guide, and branding for your solution
Analyze direct and indirect competitors to clearly articulate your solution’s differentiators and why your solution is innovative and more likely to succeed over competing options
Consult with startups to create a scope of work and fulfill UX research, UX design, product design and service design work based on your scope of work.

The application takes a few minutes to complete and will ask you to send in your resume. You do NOT need to have a UX resume or portfolio to apply - we consider folks who are at the very beginning of their career change, who are still exploring multiple career options.

You will receive UX tips and challenges via email to help you with your transition into UX and will be contacted by us if you are being considered for the apprentice program. Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ ABOUT OUR PROGRAM MANAGEMENT TEAM

Wayve’s Program Management team turns complex technical goals into coordinated delivery. Working closely with engineering, research and product teams, we align priorities, manage dependencies and bring clarity to ambiguous challenges. We combine technical depth with cross-functional leadership to help teams move faster, more effectively and with purpose-focusing on meaningful outcomes rather than process for its own sake.

As part of this team, you’ll build and lead the technical programme management function supporting our AI Platform organisation. AI Platform builds the data and compute infrastructure, model-development workflow tooling, training technology, compute management, and embedded and inference optimisation that enable Wayve’s models to be trained, iterated and deployed onto the vehicle.

The systems this organisation delivers determine how quickly Wayve can develop and ship models, how efficiently we use compute, and how well our models perform in training and on the vehicle.

🧠 Your day-to-day

- Build, coach and support a small, high-impact TPM team, helping people develop their skills, work through challenges and raise the standard of programme delivery.

- Act as a trusted delivery partner to AI Platform and Engineering leadership, aligning priorities, challenging trade-offs and holding teams accountable for meaningful outcomes.

- Work across ML and research, infrastructure, embedded and on-vehicle engineering teams, as well as cloud and vendor partners, to manage dependencies, surface risks and remove blockers.

- Use KPIs, dashboards and operational reviews to understand delivery progress, identify bottlenecks and steer decisions with the right data.

- Represent AI Platform in company-level reviews, communicating progress, risks and decisions clearly while connecting delivery to business impact.

🧩 What you’ll be working on:

- Building and scaling the technical programme management function for AI Platform, hiring to fill capability gaps and growing a high-performing team.

- Owning planning, prioritisation and execution across the AI Platform roadmap in partnership with engineering leadership.

- Leading flagship programmes across data and compute infrastructure, developer tooling, training technology, compute management, model-development workflows, and embedded and inference optimisation.

- Establishing scalable planning cadences, governance, escalation paths and operational practices that bring structure without slowing delivery.

- Driving measurable improvements in developer velocity, compute efficiency and cost, training and inference performance, and platform reliability.

- Helping engineering leaders deliver high-leverage outcomes, balancing technical trade-offs and ensuring commitments translate into impact.

🙌 You should apply if:

- You bring 8+ years of hands-on technical programme management experience across platform, infrastructure, compute, ML infrastructure, developer tooling, training or inference systems. You have built or scaled a programme function, led people and processes, and get things done with ownership and a bias for action.

- You build, coach and grow high-performing teams. You know how to develop people, hire to strengthen the team and raise the bar on technical programme management.

- You have strong technical depth across ML infrastructure, compute and embedded systems. You can engage credibly with platform and systems engineers without being expected to write production code. Your experience includes:

- A strong understanding of machine learning, GPUs, and training and inference for models from 500M to 20B

title: Direct Response Copywriter (Women’s Health)
description:
Copywriter (Women’s Health)
Eyeball Grabber Wanted: You’ve written ads that interrupted the scroll. Emails that earned the click. Landing pages that made the offer feel obvious. Video scripts that hooked fast and held attention. And sales copy that turned complicated product benefits into simple, human, persuasive messages. You know how to write with empathy, clarity, proof, and punch. You can take a clinical study, a customer insight, a product USP, or a messy brief and turn it into copy that feels easy to read and hard to ignore.
If that sounds like you, here’s your next big opportunity:
We want a Copywriter to help us write high-performing, conversion-focused copy across ads, emails, sales pages, social, video scripts, blogs, and more.
Small print here ⇒ We’re a women’s health supplement company. So if you can’t write in a way that makes women feel heard, understood, and safe enough to trust you… this isn’t the role for you.
Still here? Okay then…
This job will give you ALL the feels:
We create clinically supported, natural solutions for some of the biggest health challenges women over 40 face today. And your words will help more women discover those solutions.
Your copy will help a menopausal woman understand her body better. Feel more confident in her choices. Take action. And maybe even change the way she thinks about her health, her future, and what’s possible for her.
If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your copywriting career than here.
This job might be for you if you’ve got…
3-5 years of proven copywriting experience. When we look at your portfolio we’ll see a full-spectrum of ads, emails, landing pages, and sales pages that converted like a Kentucky Tent Revival. There’s no doubt about it… your copy SELLS!
Direct response chops that make your words cut through the clutter. You know how to write hooks, leads, headlines, subject lines, bullets, offers, calls-to-action, and sales arguments that pull people in and keep them reading. If you can make a reader think, “Okay, I need to know where this is going,” we want to talk.
A Makepeace-like ability to turn product features into customer benefits. You don’t stop at “contains calcium, magnesium, boron, and vitamin D3.” You ask: Why does that matter? What does the customer already believe? What are they afraid of? What have they tried? What do they need to understand before this feels worth buying?
A brain that can find the story in the science. You dig through a database of clinical studies, spot the strongest marketing nuggets, and turn them into a compelling product story. You don’t just summarize research. You connect the ingredients, doses, mechanisms, and results in a way that is clear, accurate, persuasive, and easy for a real human to understand. Bonus points if you’ve done this in health, wellness, supplements, or women’s health.
A performance-driven approach to writing. You don’t treat copy like precious art carved into marble. You want to know what worked, what didn’t, and what to test next. CTR, CVR, CPA, open rate, click rate, rankings, traffic, revenue - these numbers don’t bruise your ego. They sharpen your instincts.
A full-funnel writing brain. You understand that a Meta ad, an email, a sales page, a video script, an organic post, and a blog all have different jobs. You can shift tone, format, pace, and depth depending on the channel, while keeping the message consistent and on-brand.
A strong understanding of hooks, angles, and offers. You know the difference between a headline that states a fact and a hook that creates momentum. You can find fresh angles in customer reviews, testimonials, research papers, competitor funnels, product details, and the quiet little objections most writers miss.
The ability to write both short and long. You can write a 12-word ad hook, a 90-character description, a PWAT-style email, a 6,000-word sales page, or a VSL-style script without losing the thread. You know when to be punchy, when to explain,
